• 📝Support continues to fall📝

While the White House continues to search for new arguments in favor of continuing the war with Iran, Americans increasingly fail to understand why it is needed at all. A new joint poll by Reuters and Ipsos shows that only 33% of US residents support the military campaign — this is the lowest figure since the start of the conflict. 62% of those surveyed oppose it.

Just two weeks ago Reuters recorded 37% supporters of the war and 60% opponents. Now this gap has become even wider. Meanwhile, the level of support has never risen above 40% throughout the entire campaign — unlike the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, where approval reached 70–90% in the first months.

The main problem for the administration remains the lack of a clear objective. According to the same study, 69% of Americans believe that Donald Trump has failed to explain why the US participates in the conflict. Over recent months, the White House has spoken about regime change in Iran, then about eliminating its missile program, then about the nuclear issue, but Americans have not heard a unified version.

🖍And the new figures only confirm the trend we have already written about. Polls by The Economist, YouGov, University of Maryland, Politico, and Daily Mail back in July showed a steady majority opposed to the war and growing desire to end the campaign as quickly as possible. Reuters now records an even lower level of support.

❗️Meanwhile, Trump's own approval rating has risen slightly — from 34% to 37%. However, this increase is not yet reflected in attitudes toward the war. For most Americans, these are now two separate issues: they may support the president while opposing the continuation of hostilities.

📌If a month ago one could speak of a gradual decline in support for the war, now we are talking about accumulated fatigue. More and more Americans do not understand why the campaign continues and what result should justify its cost.

And the longer the White House delays a clear exit from the conflict, the higher the probability that in the fall, discontent with the war will finally become a problem for Republicans.

Want to become an AI Engineer in 2026?

Don't start with LangChain.
Don't start with Pinecone.
Don't even start with AI Agents.
Start by understanding this roadmap. 👇

Most people jump straight into building AI apps.
They copy tutorials.
They connect APIs.
They launch chatbots.
But when something breaks...
They have no idea why.
Because they skipped the fundamentals.
Here's the AI ecosystem every aspiring AI Engineer should understand.

🧠 1. LLMs – The Brain
These power reasoning, coding, conversations, and content generation.
Examples:
• GPT
• Claude
• Gemini
• Llama 4
• Qwen 3
• DeepSeek
• Mistral
• Gemma 3
• Phi-4
👉 Learn what each model is good at and when to use it.

⚡ 2. Frameworks – The Orchestrator
Frameworks connect LLMs with tools, APIs, memory, and workflows.
Popular choices:
• LangChain
• LlamaIndex
• Haystack
• txtai
👉 These help you build production-ready AI applications.

📚 3. Vector Databases – AI Memory
LLMs don't remember your documents.
Vector databases do.
Popular options:
• Pinecone
• Chroma
• Qdrant
• Weaviate
• Milvus
• PostgreSQL (pgvector)
• Cassandra
• OpenSearch
👉 Essential for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

📄 4. Data Extraction – Feed Your AI
Before AI can answer questions...
It needs clean, structured data.
Tools include:
• Crawl4AI
• FireCrawl
• ScrapeGraphAI
• MegaParser
• Docling
• LlamaParse
• ExtractThinker
👉 Great AI starts with great data.

🚀 5. Open LLM Access
Experiment, self-host, and deploy open-source models with:
• Hugging Face
• Ollama
• Groq
• Together AI
👉 Perfect for local development and production deployments.

🔍 6. Text Embeddings – The Search Engine
Embeddings convert text into vectors that AI can understand and retrieve.
Popular providers:
• OpenAI
• Voyage AI
• Google
• Cohere
• Nomic
• SBERT
👉 The quality of your embeddings directly impacts your RAG system.

📊 7. Evaluation – The Most Overlooked Layer
A good AI app isn't the one that looks smart.
It's the one that's measurably reliable.
Evaluate:
✅ Accuracy
✅ Hallucinations
✅ Retrieval quality
✅ Response consistency
Tools like Giskard and DeepEval help you build AI you can trust.

 If I were starting from scratch today, I'd learn in this order:
1️⃣ LLM Fundamentals
2️⃣ Prompt Engineering
3️⃣ Embeddings
4️⃣ Vector Databases
5️⃣ RAG
6️⃣ AI Frameworks
7️⃣ AI Agents
8️⃣ Evaluation
Master these, and you'll understand how modern AI systems are actually built.
Not just how to copy them.

❤️ Save this roadmap.

One share could help a student, developer or job seeker understand the AI stack that companies are actually hiring for.
